requirement.original: Enter key in message input field does not send message. MultiTextInput.tsx uses submitBehavior=newline which inserts a newline before React onKeyPress handler can call preventDefault(). User verified: pressing Enter navigated to different session URL. Expected: Enter sends message, Shift+Enter adds newline.
requirement.clarified: On desktop web, pressing Enter in the message input inserts a newline instead of sending the message because submitBehavior='newline' on the TextInput causes the native textarea to process the Enter key before React's onKeyPress handler fires. The fix must intercept Enter at the DOM keydown level (before the textarea's default behavior) and call preventDefault() when Enter-to-send is active.
requirement.what: Fix Enter key to send messages on desktop web instead of inserting newlines
requirement.why: Core usability bug: users expect Enter to send messages (standard web chat UX), but the input inserts a newline instead

AgentInput.tsx: ensure existing Enter-to-send logic works with the fix
new/index.tsx: ensure new session composer Enter-to-send works with the fix

root_cause_analysis.symptom: Pressing Enter in the message input on desktop web inserts a newline instead of sending the message
root_cause_analysis.root_cause: MultiTextInput.tsx line 222 sets submitBehavior='newline' on the TextInput. On web, this translates to the native textarea processing the Enter key and inserting a newline BEFORE React's onKeyPress synthetic event fires. By the time handleKeyPress (line 87) calls e.preventDefault() on line 132, the newline is already inserted into the textarea. The onKeyPress callback in AgentInput.tsx (line 524) correctly returns true to indicate 'handled', but the damage (newline insertion) is already done.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause_commit: N/A - this is an architectural issue with React Native Web's event ordering, not introduced by a specific commit. submitBehavior='newline' has been present since the component was created.
root_cause_analysis.why_introduced: submitBehavior='newline' was set to ensure multiline input works correctly on native platforms (iOS/Android), where Enter/Return should insert newlines in a multiline TextInput.
root_cause_analysis.why_problematic: On web, the browser textarea's default behavior (insert newline on Enter) fires at the DOM level before React's synthetic onKeyPress event. React Native Web's submitBehavior='newline' reinforces this default, making it impossible to intercept and prevent via React event handlers alone.
root_cause_analysis.timeline: Present since MultiTextInput component creation. Partially mitigated by PR #854 (commit b94fbae2) which added touch device detection, but desktop web was never fixed.

research_findings.reason: Well-understood web platform issue: DOM keydown fires before React Native Web synthetic events. Standard fix is to use a ref-based DOM keydown listener with preventDefault().

development_approach.strategy: Add a web-specific DOM-level keydown event listener in MultiTextInput.tsx that fires before the textarea's default behavior. When the onKeyPress callback indicates the key was handled, call event.preventDefault() at the DOM level to block the newline insertion. This keeps the existing React Native onKeyPress API intact while fixing the event ordering issue on web.
